Taking [its lualine component as a reference](https://github.com/stevearc/overseer.nvim/blob/master/lua/lualine/components/overseer.lua), here is how I'd approach this:

- Create a file 'lua/overseer-stl.lua' inside your config directory. This will be your statusline component. Populate it with the following content:
    ```lua
    local constants = require('overseer.constants')
    local task_list = require('overseer.task_list')
    local util = require('overseer.util')
    local STATUS = constants.STATUS

    local symbols = {
      [STATUS.FAILURE] = '󰅚 ',
      [STATUS.CANCELED] = ' ',
      [STATUS.SUCCESS] = '󰄴 ',
      [STATUS.RUNNING] = '󰑮 ',
    }

    return function()
      local tasks = task_list.list_tasks()
      local tasks_by_status = util.tbl_group_by(tasks, 'status')
      local pieces = { '󰍹 ' }
      for _, status in ipairs(STATUS.values) do
        local status_tasks = tasks_by_status[status]
        if symbols[status] and status_tasks then table.insert(pieces, symbols[status] .. #status_tasks) end
      end
      return table.concat(pieces, ' ')
    end
    ```
- Instead of a single `require('mini.statusline').setup()`, define custom active active function (using [this base example as reference](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/14f81b96d850d561b6ed0c1e6715fdd724e4447f/doc/mini-statusline.txt#L86-L106)) like this:
    ```lua
    -- Make sure that 'stevearc/overseer.nvim' is loaded and set up prior to this
    local overseer_status = require('overseer-stl')

    --stylua: ignore
    local active_content = function()
      local mode, mode_hl = MiniStatusline.section_mode({ trunc_width = 120 })
      local git           = MiniStatusline.section_git({ trunc_width = 40 })
      local diff          = MiniStatusline.section_diff({ trunc_width = 75 })
      local diagnostics   = MiniStatusline.section_diagnostics({ trunc_width = 75 })
      local lsp           = MiniStatusline.section_lsp({ trunc_width = 75 })
      local filename      = MiniStatusline.section_filename({ trunc_width = 140 })
      local fileinfo      = MiniStatusline.section_fileinfo({ trunc_width = 120 })
      local location      = MiniStatusline.section_location({ trunc_width = 75 })
      local search        = MiniStatusline.section_searchcount({ trunc_width = 75 })

      local overseer = overseer_status()

      return MiniStatusline.combine_groups({
        { hl = mode_hl,                  strings = { mode } },
        { hl = 'MiniStatuslineDevinfo',  strings = { git, diff, diagnostics, lsp, overseer } },
        '%<', -- Mark general truncate point
        { hl = 'MiniStatuslineFilename', strings = { filename } },
        '%=', -- End left alignment
        { hl = 'MiniStatuslineFileinfo', strings = { fileinfo } },
        { hl = mode_hl,                  strings = { search, location } },
      })
    end

    require('mini.statusline').setup({ content = { active = active_content } })
    ```

Does this answer your question?

reply_data.body:
> side question, for `mini.statusline` is it possible to inject component on the fly?
> 
> like when overseer loads (in case of lazy loading), I will inject it's component

Sure, but needs some Lua software engineering. There are several approaches here:
- You can set `MiniStatusline.config.content.active` any time and it will take effect. So set it directly to different function when 'overseer.nvim' is loaded. With something like `MiniStatusline.config.content.active = f`.
- Make `overseer_status` global (or more precisely - not local) with initial value of `function() return '' end` and change it to the "proper" function after 'overseer.nvim' is loaded.
- Probably there are other approaches.
